item.title: Optical control of electrons in a Floquet topological insulator
item.author: Daniel M. B. LeskoTobias WeitzPeter Hommelhoff
item.content:encoded:
Driving a solid with light can create a topological insulator, but controlling its electrons has remained elusive. Optical control of electrons in a Floquet topological insulator has now been achieved in light-dressed graphene.

Daniel M. B. LeskoTobias WeitzPeter Hommelhoff

Nature Physics

item.title: Doped germanium keeps pace with the light field
item.author: Christian Heide
item.content:encoded:
Attosecond transient reflection spectroscopy reveals that doped germanium can retain a light-field-driven sub-cycle optical response, with impurity doping shifting and reshaping electron dynamics on attosecond timescales.

Christian Heide

Nature Photonics

item.title: Time to embrace new platforms
item.author: Anastasiia Vasylchenkova
item.content:encoded:
With silicon-based integrated photonics having reached commercial-level maturity, the research community is directing its efforts towards heterogeneous designs and alternative material platforms with new functionalities.

Anastasiia Vasylchenkova

Nature Photonics

item.title: Ultra-wideband electrically tuned mid-infrared on-chip parametric oscillator
item.author: Alexander Y. HwangHubert S. StokowskiAmir H. Safavi-Naeini
item.content:encoded:
A thin-film lithium niobate integrated optical parametric oscillator converts a fixed near-infrared pump into 22 THz of electrically tunable mid-infrared light, achieving both broad wavelength coverage and mode-hop-free fine-tuning.

Alexander Y. HwangHubert S. StokowskiAmir H. Safavi-Naeini

Nature Photonics

item.title: The 46 companies scrambling to commercialize fusion for energy
item.author: Neil Savage
item.content:encoded:
Whether the billions of dollars of investment will lead to an inexhaustible source of clean electrical power is not yet known.

Neil Savage

Nature

item.title: Infrared absorption spectroscopy of a single polyatomic molecular ion
item.author: Zhenlin WuTim DukaPhilipp Schindler
item.content:encoded:
Non-destructive single-molecule absorption spectroscopy is achieved by detecting photon recoil from a trapped molecular ion, enabling single-photon-sensitive measurements of molecular vibrational transitions.

Zhenlin WuTim DukaPhilipp Schindler

Nature

item.title: Frontier-technology markets are too narrow — here’s how to widen them
item.author: Luisa CorradoPaul Kattuman
item.content:encoded:
Governments need to keep their procurement processes as open as possible, or they will face risks of technological lock-in down the line.

Luisa CorradoPaul Kattuman

Nature

item.title: Sound protection for electron spins
item.author: Ryuichi Ohta
item.content:encoded:
Solid state electron spins have important practical advantages for quantum technologies, but fluctuations in their host material cause decoherence. Now, it has been shown that sound waves can extend the coherence of diamond silicon vacancy spins.

Ryuichi Ohta

Nature Physics

item.title: Antidots measure anyonic charge in graphene
item.content:encoded:
Anyons are fractionally charged quasiparticles of the quantum Hall effect, and could one day power topological quantum computers. Trapping and measuring anyons remains difficult, but quasiparticle charges have now been measured using a gate-defined antidot in bilayer graphene. For hole-conjugate states, the parity of downstream integer edge modes sets the observed charge.

Nature Physics

item.title: Daily briefing: People older than 100 have more cancer-killing cells
item.author: Flora Graham
item.content:encoded:
Killer T cells might help people to live to extraordinarily old ages. Plus, the longest-lived brain organoids so far and how mass genome-screening programmes for newborns might work.

Flora Graham

Nature

item.title: Observation of conformal field theory spectra in a quantum simulator
item.author: Xiangkai SunYuan LeManuel Endres
item.content:encoded:
Measurements on an array of optically trapped neutral atoms at a quantum phase transition provide a direct observation of the universal excitation spectrum predicted by conformal field theory.

Xiangkai SunYuan LeManuel Endres

Nature

item.title: AI tool lets researchers ‘vibe code’ in the quantum realm
item.author: Davide Castelvecchi
item.content:encoded:
An autonomous AI agent can write and execute quantum computing code, but it sometimes needs a human touch.

Davide Castelvecchi

Nature

item.title: Ultrafast electron diffraction with MeV electron source from a laser wakefield accelerator
item.author: Yu FangFei LiWei Lu
item.content:encoded:
Researchers demonstrate that a laser wakefield accelerator-based device with a miniaturized permanent magnet beamline can generate and manipulate electron beams suitable for ultrafast electron diffraction.

Yu FangFei LiWei Lu

Nature Photonics

item.title: Cold-atom comagnetometry via optical control of spin states
item.author: J.-L. ZhangW.-T. LuoZ.-T. Lu
item.content:encoded:
A cold-atom comagnetometer based on the nuclear spins of 171Yb and 173Yb is demonstrated. A spin coherence time of 60 s is achieved for both isotopes. The 171Yb–173Yb ratio of nuclear magnetic moments is determined as –0.726076(3) with a 4-ppm precision.

J.-L. ZhangW.-T. LuoZ.-T. Lu

Nature Photonics

item.title: Integrated optical isolators for broadband multi-laser operation
item.author: Kyunghun HanYiliang BaoVladimir Aksyuk
item.content:encoded:
Radio-frequency electro-optic modulation enables a broadband integrated optical isolator that is magnet-free.

Kyunghun HanYiliang BaoVladimir Aksyuk

Nature Photonics

item.title: Simple and efficient end-to-end quantum thermal and ground state preparation
item.author: Zhiyan DingYongtao ZhanLin Lin
item.content:encoded:
Preparation of thermal and ground states is needed for a number of quantum algorithms but is generally computationally difficult. Now state preparation algorithms with efficiency guarantees have been developed for an important class of model.

Zhiyan DingYongtao ZhanLin Lin

Nature Physics

item.title: Reply to: Dataset artefacts can partially drive the measured decline in disruption
item.author: Michael ParkErin LeaheyRussell J. Funk
item.content:encoded:
Michael ParkErin LeaheyRussell J. Funk

Nature

item.title: A particle made of force: physicists say they’ve found mysterious ‘glueball’
item.author: Mohana Basu
item.content:encoded:
Scientists have been predicting the existence of a particle made of gluons for a long time, but detecting it has taken decades.

Mohana Basu

Nature

item.title: Superconducting 2D cuprate with a single CuO2 plane
item.author: Hengsheng LuoDongjoon SongYuanbo Zhang
item.content:encoded:
A high-quality, pristine monolayer cuprate superconductor with a single CuO2 plane is fabricated and used to identify two quantum critical phenomena emerging between the Mott insulating phase and the superconducting phase.

Hengsheng LuoDongjoon SongYuanbo Zhang

Nature

item.title: Diamonds are a metrologist’s best friends
item.author: Anita Mary Chandran
item.content:encoded:
Owing to its exceptional characteristics, diamond finds many applications in metrology. Anita Chandran introduces us to the glittering world of natural and synthetic diamonds.

Anita Mary Chandran

Nature Physics

item.title: Time-resolved imaging of antiferromagnetic skyrmion interactions
item.author: Mona BhuktaTakaaki DohiMathias Kläui
item.content:encoded:
Understanding the time-resolved dynamics of antiferromagnetic skyrmion interactions remains a challenge, limiting control over their collective behaviour. Now their ultrafast dynamics is visualized in real time in thin-film multilayers.

Mona BhuktaTakaaki DohiMathias Kläui

Nature Physics

item.title: Perfect particle transmission through duality defects
item.author: Atsushi UedaVic Vander LindenFrank Verstraete
item.content:encoded:
Dualities between different models are an important tool in theoretical many-body physics. Here a constructive recipe is given for topological interfaces between dual models that are transparent to wavepackets but alter their properties.

Atsushi UedaVic Vander LindenFrank Verstraete

Nature Physics

item.title: Levitating sensor for magnetic fields could detect ultrafaint brain activity
item.author: Dhruv Shenai
item.content:encoded:
The device’s simple design could rival much more complex alternatives in biophysics research — and could even be used to search for dark matter.

Dhruv Shenai

Nature

item.title: Pseudogap in a Fermi–Hubbard quantum simulator
item.author: Lev Haldar KendrickAnant KaleMarkus Greiner
item.content:encoded:
A cold-atom quantum simulator reveals the pseudogap metallic state in the Hubbard model, mapping its phase diagram and advancing understanding of doped Mott insulators and high-temperature superconductivity.

Lev Haldar KendrickAnant KaleMarkus Greiner

Nature

item.title: An entangling gate for dual-rail erasure qubits
item.author: Nitish MehtaJames D. TeohRobert J. Schoelkopf
item.content:encoded:
A fast, low-error entangling gate for dual-rail cavity erasure qubits preserves a strong error hierarchy, advancing scalable quantum error correction with substantially improved fault-tolerant performance.

Nitish MehtaJames D. TeohRobert J. Schoelkopf

Nature

item.title: The recovered notes of Professor Alborough
item.author: Gemma Church
item.content:encoded:
Time for a break.

Gemma Church

Nature

item.title: Encapsulation epitaxy of air-stable 2D superconductors for quantum circuits
item.author: Xudong ZhengSameia ZamanJing Kong
item.content:encoded:
An ‘encapsulation epitaxy’ mechanism is used to grow air-stable, two-dimensional superconducting films at the interface of a 2D–3D hybrid substrate, holding promise for use in fabrication of superconducting quantum circuitry.

Xudong ZhengSameia ZamanJing Kong

Nature

item.title: Upcycling of polyvinyl chloride into polyalphaolefin lubricants
item.author: Eric Munyaneza NuwayoConnor ThompsonGuoliang Liu
item.content:encoded:
A mild chemical process upcycles polyvinyl chloride waste into polyalphaolefin lubricants with tunable properties, offering an economical route to plastic recycling and improved carbon circularity.

Eric Munyaneza NuwayoConnor ThompsonGuoliang Liu

Nature

item.title: What’s missing from the White House plan for the future of US science
item.content:encoded:
To realize ‘a new golden age for science’, the United States needs open borders and must properly fund studies in the social sciences, public health and the humanities — not just research in technology and engineering.

Nature

item.title: Extensible universal photonic quantum computing with nonlinearity
item.author: Shang YuJinzhao SunRaj B. Patel
item.content:encoded:
An extensible photonic quantum computing architecture based on a fully programmable, scalable linear-optical network has been realized, and is enhanced by two addressable modules: an inline squeezing module for injecting nonlinear resources as input states and a Kerr interaction module for implementing effective nonlinear operations.

Shang YuJinzhao SunRaj B. Patel

Nature Photonics

item.title: Breaking the power wall in programmable photonics
item.author: Hanke FengCheng Wang
item.content:encoded:
A non-volatile photonic gate array based on ferroelectric domain switching eliminates static power consumption, pointing towards scalable and energy-efficient photonic integrated circuits.

Hanke FengCheng Wang

Nature Photonics

item.title: Long-lived phonons from resonators with reduced surface interactions
item.content:encoded:
Using Brillouin-based phonon spectroscopy, surface interactions have been identified as the dominant source of phonon decoherence in crystalline media. When these interactions are reduced through chemical mechanical polishing, high-frequency bulk acoustic wave oscillators can be realized with record Q-factors and coherence times, suitable for use as long-lived solid-state quantum memories.

Nature Physics

item.title: Rotation through sound
item.author: Franklin J. Vivanco
item.content:encoded:
Detecting quantized circulation in strongly correlated matter is challenging. Now it has been shown that phononic interferometry can reveal the quantized angular momentum of a strongly interacting rotating superfluid.

Franklin J. Vivanco

Nature Physics

item.title: Daily briefing: ‘Raygun’ AI can shrink or supersize proteins
item.author: Jacob Smith
item.content:encoded:
The tool can add, remove or swap protein subunits using similar steps to natural evolution. Plus, spin qubits are back in the quantum race and the drugs that could prevent long COVID.

Jacob Smith

Nature

item.title: How silicon-chip technology is being re-engineered for quantum computing
item.author: Natalia Ares
item.content:encoded:
Two demonstrations of silicon-based quantum processors tackle the engineering challenges of building scalable quantum computers.

Natalia Ares

Nature

item.title: Underdog ‘spin qubits’ leap forward in race to a useful quantum computer
item.author: Dan Garisto
item.content:encoded:
Four independent research teams report big advances in devices built with the underestimated quantum-bit technology, including lower error rates.

Dan Garisto

Nature

item.title: Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture
item.author: Brennan UndsethNicola MeggiatoLieven M. K. Vandersypen
item.content:encoded:
A silicon spin-qubit device comprising a shuttling bus for transporting qubits is used to achieve parity checks up to weight four, highlighting the feasibility and benefits of incorporating shuttling into semiconductor quantum processors.

Brennan UndsethNicola MeggiatoLieven M. K. Vandersypen

Nature

item.title: Quantum meets capitalism: how to pair long-term bets on technology with commercial speed
item.author: Charles Tahan
item.content:encoded:
Quantum computing exists because governments funded risky bets. Capitalism can carry it the rest of the way — if quantum scientists are supported.

Charles Tahan

Nature

item.title: A digitally controlled silicon quantum processing unit
item.author: Michael AbrahamEdwin AcunaAndrew Ziegler
item.content:encoded:
A silicon quantum processing unit executes high-fidelity multiqubit circuits, with all time-varying control signals generated by a digitally programmed cryogenic complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor controller and delivered to the low-noise, exchange-only qubit device through a high-density superconducting ribbon cable.

Michael AbrahamEdwin AcunaAndrew Ziegler

Nature

item.title: The piezochiral effect
item.author: Z. ZengM. FörstP. G. Radaelli
item.content:encoded:
The piezochiral effect, a new member of the family of strain-responsive functionalities alongside piezoelectricity and piezomagnetism, is introduced, enabling control of chirality through mechanical strain, with future applications in photonics, spintronics, biosensing and quantum information.

Z. ZengM. FörstP. G. Radaelli

Nature

item.title: Enzymatic glycosylation and amidation reshapes polyene bioactivity
item.author: Saadia N. MirzaAlberto CarellaJason Micklefield
item.content:encoded:
Pathways to previously undescribed polyenes, including unusual enzymes that introduce more sugars onto polyene scaffolds, are discovered, and their accessibility through clean and efficient fermentation and potential for safe use as antifungal treatments is described.

Saadia N. MirzaAlberto CarellaJason Micklefield

Nature

item.title: All living things emit a faint glow. Could this light be useful?
item.author: Jo Marchant
item.content:encoded:
Ultra-weak ‘biophotons’ might be used to diagnose disease, or could even represent a new signalling mechanism in cells.

Jo Marchant

Nature

item.title: Topological phase transitions and mixed-state order in a Hubbard quantum simulator
item.author: Lin SuRahul SahayMarkus Greiner
item.content:encoded:
Topological phases can be hard to distinguish with local measurements. Now, a transition between two such phases has been revealed in ultracold erbium atoms, and shown to disappear when two systems are stacked or information about disorder is lost.

Lin SuRahul SahayMarkus Greiner

Nature Physics

item.title: Daily briefing: Orcas smash sunfish to smithereens
item.author: Jacob Smith
item.content:encoded:
The dolphins might be helping their young eat, or just having fun. Plus, the beauty and skill of scientific illustration and a crash course in quantum computing.

Jacob Smith

Nature

item.title: Manipulating spin dynamics via exciton–exciton interactions for bright spin light-emitting diodes
item.author: Qi LiuYanlong WangShaocong Hou
item.content:encoded:
Modulating exciton–exciton interactions in hybrid chiral metal halide heterostructures suppresses spin relaxation, enabling spin light-emitting diodes that directly emit circularly polarized light with a dissymmetry factor of 0.2 and a half-lifetime of 5,000 h at an initial luminance of 100 cd m−2.

Qi LiuYanlong WangShaocong Hou

Nature Photonics

item.title: How do quantum computers work?
item.author: Dan FoxDavide Castelvecchi
item.content:encoded:
Recent breakthroughs suggest usable devices could be here in a decade.

Dan FoxDavide Castelvecchi

Nature

item.title: Capturing the first moments after high-energy molecular impact
item.content:encoded:
When high-energy particles, such as photons, electrons or ions, collide with a molecule, the collision kicks off processes that occur within the first femtoseconds after impact. Quantum mechanical motion of electrons bound to the molecule, which ultimately breaks chemical bonds, has now been captured using an attosecond X-ray free-electron laser.

Nature Physics

item.title: Non-Gaussian statistics of the order parameter across a phase transition
item.author: Maxime AllemandGéraud DupuyDavid Clément
item.content:encoded:
Single-atom measurements show non-Gaussian order-parameter fluctuations and critical scaling across a continuous phase transition, highlighting the importance of full statistical distributions in understanding universality.

Maxime AllemandGéraud DupuyDavid Clément

Nature

item.title: Semiconducting and magnetic lanthanide MXenes from intercalated halides
item.author: Qian FangLiming WangQing Huang
item.content:encoded:
A bottom-up synthesis strategy creates lanthanide MXenes (Ln2CT2) that combine semiconducting behaviour with ferromagnetism, offering a promising new class of two-dimensional materials for spintronic applications.

Qian FangLiming WangQing Huang

Nature

item.title: Beyond quantum linear optics with adaptive boson sampling
item.author: Giovanni RodariTommaso FrancalanciFabio Sciarrino
item.content:encoded:
An adaptive boson sampling architecture is developed to achieve optical evolutions beyond the usual quantum linear optics set-ups via measurement-based feedback. A set of witnesses to certify the nonlinear-optical evolution is provided.

Giovanni RodariTommaso FrancalanciFabio Sciarrino

Nature Photonics
